name: InterfaceDescriptor

fields.name: name
fields.comment:
name is the name of the interface. It should be a short-name (without
 a period) such that the fully qualified name of the interface will be
 package.name, ex. for the package a.b and interface named C, the
 fully-qualified name will be a.b.C.

fields.name: description
fields.comment:
description is a human-readable description of the interface and its
 purpose.

comment:
InterfaceDescriptor describes an interface type to be used with
 accepts_interface and implements_interface and declared by declare_interface.

name: ScalarDescriptor

fields.name: name
fields.comment:
name is the name of the scalar. It should be a short-name (without
 a period) such that the fully qualified name of the scalar will be
 package.name, ex. for the package a.b and scalar named C, the
 fully-qualified name will be a.b.C.

fields.name: description
fields.comment:
description is a human-readable description of the scalar and its
 encoding format. For instance a big integer or decimal scalar should
 specify precisely the expected encoding format.

fields.name: field_type
fields.comment:
field_type is the type of field with which this scalar can be used.
 Scalars can be used with one and only one type of field so that
 encoding standards and simple and clear. Currently only string and
 bytes fields are supported for scalars.

comment:
ScalarDescriptor describes an scalar type to be used with
 the scalar field option and declared by declare_scalar.
 Scalars extend simple protobuf built-in types with additional
 syntax and semantics, for instance to represent big integers.
 Scalars should ideally define an encoding such that there is only one
 valid syntactical representation for a given semantic meaning,
 i.e. the encoding should be deterministic.

name: PageRequest

fields.name: key
fields.comment:
key is a value returned in PageResponse.next_key to begin
 querying the next page most efficiently. Only one of offset or key
 should be set.

fields.name: offset
fields.comment:
offset is a numeric offset that can be used when key is unavailable.
 It is less efficient than using key. Only one of offset or key should
 be set.

fields.name: limit
fields.comment:
limit is the total number of results to be returned in the result page.
 If left empty it will default to a value to be set by each app.

fields.name: count_total
fields.comment:
count_total is set to true  to indicate that the result set should include
 a count of the total number of items available for pagination in UIs.
 count_total is only respected when offset is used. It is ignored when key
 is set.

fields.name: reverse
fields.comment:
reverse is set to true if results are to be returned in the descending order.

 Since: cosmos-sdk 0.43

name: PageResponse

fields.name: next_key
fields.comment:
next_key is the key to be passed to PageRequest.key to
 query the next page most efficiently. It will be empty if
 there are no more results.

fields.name: total
fields.comment:
total is total number of results available if PageRequest.count_total
 was set, its value is undefined otherwise

name: CollateralAuction
comment:
CollateralAuction is a two phase auction.
 Initially, in forward auction phase, bids can be placed up to a max bid.
 Then it switches to a reverse auction phase, where the initial amount up for auction is bid down.
 Unsold Lot is sent to LotReturns, being divided among the addresses by weight.
 Collateral auctions are normally used to sell off collateral seized from CDPs.

name: DebtAuction
comment:
DebtAuction is a reverse auction that mints what it pays out.
 It is normally used to acquire pegged asset to cover the CDP system's debts that were not covered by selling
 collateral.
